newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy offers 700 mln ord shares in Eni sale.
newsitem.headline: Italy offers 700 mln ord shares in Eni sale.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Sunday that it was offering a total of 700 million ordinary shares in the second tranche of the sale of state-controlled energy group Eni.
A Treasury statement said a minimum of 250 million of the ordinary shares would be offered in a public sale offer (OPV) and up to 25 percent of that was destined for Eni employees.
Shares in the OPV will be sold at a discount to the market rate and the price is to be announced on October 20, the day before the second flotation is launched.
The Treasury said there was also the possibility of additional shares under a "green shoe" arrangement, which allows institutional investors to receive additional stock to that already on offer.
This would be up to a maximum of 15 percent of the global offer, or 105 million shares, the Treasury said.
More details of the second tranche sale are due to be announced at a Treasury news conference on Monday.
Last year, the Treasury sold a first 15 percent tranche of Eni, which has a market capitalisation of some $35 billion and is Italy's largest publicly traded company.
It was floated last November at 5,250 lire to trade in Milan, London and New York and closed trade on Friday in Milan 3.02 percent up at 7,302 lire after a year's high of 7,925 lire.
The government has indicated it might use the proceeds from the second tranche sale to reduce Italy's budget deficit rather than state debt.
